claim: Free-shape stochastic hill climbing on the height array (block, sparse, and bump multiplicative perturbations with adaptive noise and restarts) beats the constant seed substantially, reaching R=0.784 from 2/3 on a 1600-point grid, versus 0.735 for the structured analytic-family route. The winning shape is unimodal-ish but not flat: peak height ~2.35x the mean, f*f maximum off-center at 0.61 of sup

Scanning truncated Gaussian, power, and few-block families by exact R and then refining parameters and heights gives a solid structured gain to R=0.735 from 2/3, with a near-symmetric shape (peak at 0.52 of support, max/mean height 1.88) and a broader f*f than the free-search result (only 11% of knots within 5% of max). It is a reliable but weaker route than free-shape search, useful mainly as a s

Block-coordinate ascent (line-searched multiplicative scaling of contiguous blocks plus smooth global tilts, with upsampling between levels) is a stronger local search than sparse random perturbations on the p0003 basin: it pushed R from 0.784437 to 0.784576 at N=12800 (p0004) and a smooth-block variant reached 0.784634 (p0006), both above the 0.78440 that p0003's sparse method reached at N=1600.

Running the block-coordinate multigrid search on p0002's smooth N=4000 state lifted it from 0.735114 to 0.783098 (p0005), nearly matching the p0003 basin. So p0002's deficit was mostly resolution/weak polish, not a worse basin: the same optimizer recovers almost the same R from a very different starting shape (its f*f peak sits at 0.635 vs 0.387 for p0004), suggesting the optimum is broad and reac

Re-parametrizing f by a small number of control heights and searching those globally (differential evolution plus Nelder-Mead restarts, mirrored) at coarse N, then refining and upsampling to N=12800, escapes the 0.7846 free-shape basin and reaches R=0.8468 — a +0.062 jump, far larger than any polish gain. An L-BFGS-B polish on log h with an analytic gradient of R (argmax knot fixed) interleaved with upsampling and stochastic climbs gives only a tiny gain (+0.00048, 0.784634 to 0.785114 at N=102400) on the p0006 basin. So gradient polish is a reliable but marginal local finisher; it does not escape the basin, confirming that the binding factor is shape/basin rather than local smoothness.

Raising the control resolution of the low-dimensional parametrization (K from ~12 up to 16/24/32/48) and re-searching locally around the resampled controls at moderate N, then refining and upsampling, escapes the K≈12 ceiling: on p0007's basin it lifted R from 0.846790 to 0.858076 (+0.0113) at N=12800. Analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B polish on log h at fixed argmax knot, interleaved with block climb and one upsample to 25600, adds essentially nothing on the p0007 basin: +0.000013 (0.846790 to 0.846803) at N=12800. Combined with the earlier tiny +0.00048 on the p0006 basin, fine-grid gradient polish is locally saturated once a good basin is found — the binding factor is basin/shape, not fine-grid slac

Extending the control resolution of the low-dimensional parametrization beyond K=48 (to K=64/96/128) with wider search bounds and more restarts still adds real gain: on p0010's basin it lifted R from 0.858076 to 0.864436 (+0.00636) at N=1600, so K=48 was not the ceiling and control resolution remains a live lever.

Reordering the control-resolution search to run the highest resolutions (K=128,96,64) first with hard per-K time slices, and dropping differential evolution for cheap local Nelder-Mead in control space, does add gain on the p0012 basin: R rose from 0.864436 to 0.864671 (+0.000235) at N=12800. Reordering the p0021 stages to spend most budget on fine full-N block climbs from best with small kicks (smoothing demoted to escape) adds nothing: 0.864846 to 0.864846 (+0.000000). Budget allocation among the existing climb/smooth moves is not the binding constraint on this basin — the shape itself is at a local optimum for those moves.
